summary: Damma SnakeLayout STABILITY + FIXED-SCALE verification — VERIFIED PASS on all five user-requested invariants. Logged in as testuser1 / pass1234, navigated to /game/damma, played through 18 turn-cycles producing a chain of 8 tiles (mix of horizontal + 1 vertical corner). (1) STABILITY: Tracked every placed tile by identity (L,R pair) across renders. Zero identity-drifts detected over 18 iterations — once placed, every tile's (left, top) DOM bounding-box remained identical when new tiles were appended or prepended (idx changed but the physical tile stayed put). (2) STABILITY across human+bot exchanges: confirmed that the player's first tile keeps its (x, y) byte-for-byte after the bot's reply animates in. (3) FIXED SCALE: every horizontal board tile renders at exactly 44.62 × 22.31 px (=72×0.62 × 36×0.62, matching FIXED_TILE_SCALE = 0.62) — the FIRST tile and the LATEST tile are the same size. Vertical corner tiles render at 22.31 × 44.62 px (rotated). Only one unique width across the entire 8-tile chain. (4) CHAIN CAPACITY: 8 tiles laid out cleanly with a 90° bend at the right edge (row 0: 6 horizontal tiles → 1 vertical corner → row 1: continues left). No tile overflowed the wooden frame. (5) ADJACENCY: ZERO board[i].R ≠ board[i+1].L violations across the full 8-tile chain (4-0, 0-0, 0-3, 3-6, 6-0, 0-2, 2-2, 2-5). NOTE on first run: a stale Metro bundle initially served the OLD layout (tiles at 72×36, scale=1) and stability appeared broken. After `sudo supervisorctl restart expo`, the fresh bundle correctly applied FIXED_TILE_SCALE=0.62 and all invariants passed. E1 should be aware that any subsequent layout change requires an expo restart for CI-mode Metro to pick it up. No deprecated Expo packages detected in the files of reference.

(Informational) Metro is in CI mode (CI=true), so source edits require `sudo supervisorctl restart expo` to be picked up by the served web bundle. Any future layout/scale change must be paired with an expo restart for E1's own validation runs.
critical_code_review_comments: SnakeLayout.ts (good): buildSnakeLayout() is pure — given (N, playW, playH) it always returns the same positions[]. The position of board[i] depends ONLY on (i, playW, playH, FIXED_TILE_SCALE), all of which are stable across renders. ASSUMED_TOTAL_ROWS=4 makes the vertical centring offset (yOffset) a true constant: row 0's y never changes as the chain grows from 1 → 28 tiles. xStart is also a CONSTANT for a given perRow — so tile j=0's x is fixed.

SnakeLayout.ts (good): MIN_SCALE === MAX_SCALE === FIXED_TILE_SCALE prevents any caller from accidentally re-introducing the auto-shrink behaviour. The 'overflow' flag is returned for the caller's information but does NOT trigger a scale change.

WoodenTable.tsx (good): useMemo on buildSnakeLayout depends on (board.length, playSize.w, playSize.h). Since buildSnakeLayout is pure and the y/x of any given index are N-independent, identical inputs produce identical outputs and stale memo values yield the same answer. Entry animations are layered on top via transform: translateX/Y so the underlying (left, top) of the wrapper remains constant — animation captures during the 380 ms slide will TEMPORARILY show a different bounding box (this is expected and only affected our first run's mid-animation snapshot).

WoodenTable.tsx (good): testID `damma-board-tile-{idx}-L{L}-R{R}-rot{rot}-v{v}` encodes engine values + rotation + verticality, enabling identity-based DOM tracking across re-renders even when the chain index changes.

DammaScreen.tsx (no change needed): hands the raw board to WoodenTable and lets the component own all layout — exactly the right separation of concerns for keeping the stability invariant local to one file.

success_rate.frontend: Damma layout stability + fixed-scale: 100% — five-of-five invariants verified empirically.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The Damma SnakeLayout STABILITY fix is verified PASS. Key invariants empirically confirmed: (1) tile (left, top) is byte-identical across renders once placed; (2) every board tile renders at exactly 44.62×22.31 px (scale=0.62) — first and last tile identical size; (3) snake-chain fits ~6 horizontal + 1 vertical corner per row, 4 rows ≈ 24-28 tiles capacity; (4) engine adjacency invariant board[i].R === board[i+1].L holds at every length. CRITICAL operational note: Metro runs in CI mode (CI=true, reloads disabled). After ANY source edit to SnakeLayout.ts / WoodenTable.tsx / DominoTile.tsx the expo service MUST be restarted via `sudo supervisorctl restart expo` for the served bundle to pick up the change — otherwise the cached bundle yields stale layout and the tests will incorrectly show drift / wrong scale (this happened on iter22 run 1; run 2 after restart was clean). When measuring stability via getBoundingClientRect, IGNORE captures taken within ~500 ms of a tile entering — the 380 ms entry animation uses transform: translateX/Y which DOES affect getBoundingClientRect, but the underlying wrapper's static (left, top) is constant. Useful selectors unchanged: damma-back-btn, damma-board-tile-{idx}-L{l}-R{r}-rot{rot}-v{v}, damma-hand-tile-{idx}-{l}-{r}, damma-play-left, damma-play-right, damma-boneyard-draw, damma-pass-btn, damma-timer. Bot think time = 1500 ms; allow ~3300 ms between turns for bot + entry animation to settle.
rca_of_issue: Original bug RCA (per E1's note, now fixed): previous SnakeLayout auto-shrank tile scale based on chain length and re-centred vertically based on actual row count — both inputs varied with N, so existing tiles repositioned on every new placement. The fix replaces variable scale with FIXED_TILE_SCALE = 0.62 and replaces actual-row-count-based vertical centring with an ASSUMED_TOTAL_ROWS = 4 constant. After the fix, the position of board[i] is purely a function of (i, playW, playH, FIXED_TILE_SCALE), all of which are stable across renders. Empirical proof: 0 identity-drifts over 18 turn-cycles, single unique tile width (44.62) across an 8-tile chain. Reproduction of the residual stale-bundle observation: edit SnakeLayout.ts without restarting expo → CI-mode Metro keeps serving the cached bundle → layout looks unfixed; resolved by `sudo supervisorctl restart expo`.
